road noun

also roads, highway, on the road, street, country road

classical

via, viae f.

noun, first declension · Declension on Wiktionary

road, way; a street

The ordinary word for any road, in town or country; the great highways are viae with names (via Appia).

Other words

  • iter, itineris n. — the way one takes, a route; a journey

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 4.3.4: iter dēvium, a side road (Lewis & Short s.v. dēvius); M-O s.v. road: backroad, secondary road; Traupman 404: way (route), iter · Declension on Wiktionary

    The going, or the route taken, more than the road itself.

  • vīcus, vīcī m. — a street lined with houses, in a town; a village

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Cic. Mil. 64; Hor. Ep. 1.20.18 (Lewis & Short) · Declension on Wiktionary

  • strāta, strātae f. — a paved road

    noun, first declension · also used · late Latin · Eutr. 9.15 (Lewis & Short s.v. sternō); M-O s.v. road: paved road; Traupman 218: street (paved) · Declension on Wiktionary

    Short for via strāta, a paved road; the source of English street.

Examples

  • postera tempestās melior, via pejor

    the next day the weather was better, the road worseHor. S. 1.5.96

  • tantum lutī tōtā viā fuit ut possim vidērī nihilōminus nāvigāsse

    there was so much mud the whole way that I might as well have gone by seaSen. Ep. 57.1

  • omnis enim fermē via praeceps, angusta, lūbrica erat

    for almost the whole road was steep, narrow and slipperyLiv. 21.35.11–12

  • via regiōnālis

    a country roadTraupman 298

  • platēa

    a street (with houses)Traupman 386
